observed_facts: Both affected claims originate in FORTNA/Conveyor.asc and have the identical address tuple word 1070, bit 3.
Raw Configio rows for word 1070 identify Low bank 144 as 1794-IB16; the independent hardware bank map places 1794-IB16 input bank 144 in the same rack/module context.

The High half at bank 145 has no hardware-bank match. Independent traces for words 100 and 101 show that a matched Low half with an unmatched High half is a normal one-sided-binding shape, not evidence to bind the High half to a different module.
candidate.candidate_rule_description: When raw physical claims share an identical Configio word-and-bit address and the independently derived directional bank/catalog join yields only one module context, retain the shared context as evidence but do not choose an owning claim. Emit REVIEW_REQUIRED for every colliding claim.

preconditions: at least two distinct claim_ids have the same machine, word, and bit
exact directional bank match and catalog compatibility identify a single module context

proposed_transformation: Group raw physical claims by machine, word, and bit.
Independently bind the Configio half only by exact directional bank and catalog compatibility.
If group cardinality is greater than one, preserve all claims and set their disposition to REVIEW_REQUIRED; do not select a winner from name, source-row order, or description.
Do not infer a match from an unmatched opposite LoHi half.

supporting_examples.independent_binding_evidence: word 1070 Low bank 144 matches the 1794-IB16 input-bank entry; both claims collide on the same tuple.

counterexamples.observation: Low bank 130 is accepted while High bank 131 has no bank match; it binds an output module, not an input module.
Low bank 132 is accepted while High bank 133 has no bank match; it independently repeats the one-sided pattern.
High bank 145 has no bank match and must not be used to select a different module or claim owner.

ambiguities: Only one duplicate-owner address tuple is present in this cluster, so evidence supports a narrow collision-handling guard rather than a broad ownership-precedence convention.
The raw source does not contain evidence establishing whether either label is the intended operational owner.
additional_evidence_needed: Authoritative Fortna source documentation or a verified design artifact that defines ownership precedence between duplicate word/bit claims, if an owner is to be selected.
tests_required: Verify all physical claims are grouped by machine, word, and bit before any owner-selection step.
Confirm the candidate leaves the two word-1070 bit-3 claims in REVIEW_REQUIRED and creates no winner.
Regression-test words 100 and 101 to confirm unmatched High halves do not cross-bind.
Reject any candidate that chooses an owner using source-row order, IO name, or description.

confidence.basis: The duplicate raw address is direct-source evidence, and the hardware/configio join is corroborated by independent aggregate and rack evidence; no raw evidence supports owner precedence.
